report:
### Conclusion
The claim that abaloparatide reduces vertebral fractures in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis is **true**, supported by high-quality clinical evidence.

### Evidence Behind the Claim
* **ACTIVE Phase 3 Trial:** In the pivotal Abaloparatide Comparator Trial in Vertebral Endpoints (ACTIVE), daily subcutaneous abaloparatide led to an 86% relative risk reduction in new vertebral fractures compared to placebo over 18 months (https://www.mdedge.com/obgyn/article/137158/osteoporosis/fda-approves-abaloparatide-postmenopausal-osteoporosis, https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2544640).
* **Systematic Reviews & Meta-Analyses:** Quantitative evidence across systematic reviews demonstrates that abaloparatide substantially lowers vertebral fracture risk (relative risk 0.13–0.21) while significantly increasing lumbar spine bone mineral density compared to placebo controls (https://read.qxmd.com/read/41598611/the-efficacy-and-safety-of-abaloparatide-in-osteoporosis-a-systematic-review-and-meta-analysis).
* **Regulatory Authorization:** Based on these clinical endpoints, the U.S. FDA approved abaloparatide (Tymlos) specifically for postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at high fracture risk, recognizing its proven reduction in vertebral fracture risk (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208743lbl.pdf).

Rigorous clinical data consistently confirms abaloparatide's effectiveness in preventing vertebral fractures in this population.
